moat_against: P&C policies are re-shopped at renewal — low policyholder switching costs and agents can place business elsewhere
Pricing power is cyclical: Q2 2026 combined ratio rose to 100.8% and operating income fell 28% YoY as competition intensified
Catastrophe exposure is structural — Q2 2026 Ohio catastrophe losses were nearly 4x the state's 5-year Q2 average
Net income is dominated by equity-portfolio fair-value swings, not underwriting (2022 net loss on revenue of $6.56B in the filed history)
Capable national rivals (Travelers, Progressive, Chubb and others) contest the same agency business
moat_for: Independent-agent distribution network built since 1950, with local-agent relationships competitors cannot replicate quickly
Disciplined underwriting: 14 consecutive years of P&C underwriting profit through FY2025, FY2025 combined ratio 94.9%
Conservative balance sheet and long dividend-growth record supporting agent and policyholder trust through cycles
Diversified P&C, life, excess & surplus and reinsurance lines across 46 states smooths single-line cycles
Large investment portfolio and rising investment income (+14% in FY2025) provide a second earnings engine
moat_justification: Disciplined P&C underwriter with a loyal independent-agent network, 14 consecutive years of underwriting profit through FY2025 (FY2025 combined ratio 94.9%) and a long dividend-growth record — but P&C cover is re-shopped at renewal with low policyholder switching costs, pricing is cyclical, catastrophe losses are a permanent tail, and earnings are dominated by a large equity-investment portfolio rather than a defensible underwriting franchise; moderate/narrow moat, CAP 8.5y.
name: Cincinnati Financial Corporation
one_liner: Disciplined P&C insurer with a loyal agency network, moat 5/10 — clears 15% on TTM owner's earnings (18.4% weighted, IV@15% $214.99 vs $166.67) but the Finance sector-model mismatch and a TTM base well above the 3-yr median keep confidence low; a margin of safety against the bear case needs ~$161 or below.
